findings.title: The new 2^40 wrap-bound rejection row is dead-on-arrival: check_reject_balance's entire 79-row table passes vacuously (the helper omits the crises source), and the row's value/rule pair could never match anyway
findings.location: core/catalog_test.odin:887 (row), :997-1015 (check_reject_balance helper), core/catalog.odin:1166-1170 (production rule), core/catalog.odin:1813 (jint_strict -> i32)
findings.evidence: Perkins mutation probes: replacing the row's expected rule with 'ZZZ_PROBE_RULE' keeps the suite 297/297 GREEN; instrumenting the helper shows all 79 balance rows reject with file='crises.json' rule='invalid JSON' (empty crises source) and return through the non-balance trivial branch; jint_strict returns i32 so 2^40 overflows to 'clock keys must be integers' and di=2^40 does not trip '> (1<<40)'
findings.detail: A gate that cannot fail pins nothing (the vacuous-pin doctrine). The PR's balance fail-fast surface — including all 6 box clock rows and the new wrap bound — is unpinned at this sha; a revert of any balance rule ships green.
findings.recommended_fix: Set crises = CRISES_VALID in the helper (one line, mirroring check_reject_eras); make the row actually exercise the 2^40 branch (value 2^40+1 past the i32-bound question, or widen the clock-key parse) and assert the exact rule.
